names: French Mandate for Syria and Lebanon
title: French Mandate for Syria and Lebanon
capsule: The French Mandate for Syria and Lebanon was awarded to France by the League of Nations in 1920, formalizing control over former Ottoman territories that French forces had occupied following the Arab Revolt and World War I armistice. France subdivided the mandate into several administrative units—Greater Lebanon, the State of Syria, and separate autonomous regions for the Alawites and the Jabal Druze—using a divide-and-rule approach that privileged Christian and minority communities. Nationalist resistance culminated in the Great Syrian Revolt (1925–1927), which France suppressed by bombing Damascus. Britain pressured France to grant independence during World War II; Lebanon gained independence in 1943 and Syria in 1946, completing the mandate's dissolution.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Mandate boundaries are defined in League of Nations documents and are well attested; internal administrative subdivisions changed several times and their precise limits require careful periodization.
